headline: A quiet weekend for prices but not for Nvidia: the New York Times says the SEC is looking at its accounting, and the short week turns on ADI Tuesday and a crowded Wednesday.
summary: No market traded this weekend, so every price here is the Friday Nov 20 close (the dashboard's prices_as_of is 2026-11-20). The one real weekend story: the New York Times reported Saturday that the SEC is looking into Nvidia's accounting practices, at an early stage, and that the inquiry could end with no charges (AFP). A correction to Saturday's brief: the SEC probe was first reported by the Wall Street Journal on Nov 17, not on Friday afternoon (InvestmentNews). No extension of China's Nov 27 metals pause was found, and no Fed official spoke over the weekend. New for this week: the Beige Book lands Wednesday at 2pm ET after the 8:30am reports, and MSCI adds Anthropic to its big indexes at the Nov 30 close. Stock futures open at 6pm ET Sunday and were not available when this was written.

regime.why: Nothing traded since Friday's close, so the picture has not changed. The weekend news added to the Nvidia overhang rather than easing it. Monday's open is the first test.

signals.title: Nvidia: the SEC inquiry reportedly covers its accounting, and Saturday's timeline needs a fix
signals.since_yesterday: The New York Times reported Saturday that the SEC is looking into Nvidia's accounting practices and that the inquiry is at an early stage (AFP). Also, the first SEC report was the Wall Street Journal on Nov 17, not Friday as Saturday's brief said.
signals.what_happened: Citing people briefed on it, the New York Times said Saturday that the SEC inquiry into Nvidia is at an early stage, covers its accounting practices, and could end with no charges (AFP, Nov 22). It is not clear whether it ties to the Huang scandal or to a reporting change: Nvidia moved its sales by region from where customers are billed to where they are headquartered, and Singapore dropped out of the breakdown (AFP). Singapore had been $10.2 billion, 22% of revenue, in the quarter ended July 2025 (Fortune). On Friday President Trump said he would "love to see Jensen be given a second chance"; the board has said it does not intend to reinstate him (AFP; ABC News). Our correction: the Wall Street Journal first reported an SEC probe on Nov 17 (InvestmentNews). Saturday's brief tied Friday's 14% drop to a new report that afternoon; we could not confirm what new fact came out Friday.
signals.so_what: An accounting question is slower to clear than a leadership scandal: it can mean restated numbers or new disclosure, and buyers tend to wait until it is settled. Who pays: Nvidia, and suppliers whose sales lean on its orders. Second order: other chip and server makers that bill Asian customers through hubs like Singapore may get the same question. What would make this wrong: the SEC closing the inquiry quickly, which AFP says is possible. The next dates are Treasury Secretary Bessent's request on Nov 17 for answers from the board within 10 days, so about Nov 27 (InvestmentNews), and Huang's closed door House interview on Dec 1 (ABC News).
signals.for_you: Swing: no chip entries this week. Puts: a VIX near 36 makes chip premiums look rich, but the group is falling, so the put rules say no NVDA or chip puts. Long term: NVDA is not on the long term scan buy list, and ANET, ADI and ENTG stay off it until they close back over their points.

signals.title: This week: what is new since Saturday's calendar
signals.what_happened: Added since Saturday: the Beige Book at 2pm ET Wednesday and a 5 year note auction at 1pm ET Tuesday (Traders and Quants). Sunday consensus from Yahoo Finance: October core PCE +0.3% for the month and 3.2% for the year (prior 3.1%); headline 3.8% (prior 3.6%); Q3 GDP 3.5% (the earlier estimate was 3.4%, which Saturday's brief listed as the forecast); durable goods +0.5%; personal spending +0.4%; Conference Board confidence 92.1. The Fed's quiet period starts Saturday Nov 28, so Wednesday's data gets the last word before Dec 9 (Traders and Quants). At the Nov 30 close MSCI adds Anthropic to the large cap part of its global indexes and removes Strategy (MSTR) (Newsquawk; Cointelegraph). China's pause on its gallium, germanium and antimony ban to the US still ends Nov 27; no extension notice was found as of Nov 22. Stock futures had not opened when this was written.
signals.so_what: Wednesday now carries five 8:30am reports, new home sales at 10am, the 7 year auction at 11:30am and the Beige Book at 2pm, all the day before a holiday on thin volume. A hot core PCE (0.4% or more) would push yields up and take away the one hedge that worked last week. Second order of the MSCI change: index funds must buy Anthropic at the Nov 30 close, and part of that money comes out of other large tech names in the same funds.
signals.for_you: Swing: do not act on Monday's open. WM's phone alerts are live (trigger 247.90, void 238.20; it closed 239.63 on Nov 20), and so is SO's range up alert at 94.94. Monday's run resets the range alerts. Puts: the AEP 120 Dec 18 idea waits for Monday's put screen. Long term: ABBV, LMT and V are the names at or over their points; no first pieces before Wednesday's PCE.

history.what: Bespoke counts only five weeks with an S&P 500 loss every day and four drops of 1% or more, these two among them; both times stocks made lower lows months later (Yahoo Finance, Nov 21, 2026).
history.lesson: One violent week rarely marks the low by itself.

principle.text: Be radically open minded: hold your view, but look hard for what would prove it wrong (paraphrase of Principles).
